subject: physics_2
question_text: What is Greenhouse effect and its contribution towards the surface temperature of earth?

mark_split.label: Gases absorb and re-emit the infrared

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: the surface absorbs incoming short-wavelength solar radiation and re-emits long-wavelength infrared; greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, water vapour) absorb that infrared and re-emit part of it downward, raising the average surface temperature. The book (p.42) says the infrared is 'reflected back' by the clouds and gases — the correct mechanism is absorption and re-emission, and the card writes it that way, recording the book's wording in the s3 why.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: What the greenhouse effect is
lines: Greenhouse gases in the atmosphere absorb
the infrared radiation that the Earth's
surface emits and send part of it back
toward the surface. The heating of the
surface and the atmosphere produced this
way is called the greenhouse effect.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the effect and the radiation it works on — infrared.
steps.why: The definition must contain the mechanism in miniature: gases, infrared from the surface, and part of it returned. A definition without the word infrared reads as any kind of heating.
common_mistakes: Defining it with a glasshouse picture only. The exam answer is about the atmosphere: gases returning the infrared the surface emits.
Saying the gases stop sunlight from leaving. Sunlight comes in; what the gases absorb is the infrared the surface emits.

recall.must_convey: That greenhouse gases absorb the infrared the surface emits and send part of it back, heating the surface and atmosphere.
accept: gases absorb infrared from the earth
send it back to the surface
heating of the surface and atmosphere

steps.memory_tip: Three verbs in order: absorb, re-emit, warm.

steps.label: Sunlight in, infrared out
lines: Solar radiation reaches the Earth mostly
as short-wavelength visible radiation.
The surface absorbs it, warms, and then
emits the energy as long-wavelength
infrared radiation.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The wavelength change — short in, long out — is the point of this step.
steps.why: The wavelength change is what lets the atmosphere treat the two flows differently: it is nearly transparent to the incoming short waves and absorbing for the outgoing infrared.
common_mistakes: Writing that the surface reflects the sunlight. Reflected light would leave unchanged; the surface absorbs the energy and emits it again as infrared.
Leaving out the wavelengths. Short in and long out is what this mark is for.

recall.must_convey: That the surface absorbs short-wavelength solar radiation and emits long-wavelength infrared.
accept: short wavelength in long wavelength out

steps.memory_tip: Short waves come down; long waves go up.

steps.label: The gases absorb and re-emit
steps.mark_note: CO₂, CH₄, N₂O absorb and re-emit
lines: Greenhouse gases such as CO₂, CH₄, N₂O
and water vapour absorb this outgoing
infrared radiation and re-emit it in all
directions, so part of it returns to the
surface instead of escaping into space.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Name at least two gases and use the pair absorb and re-emit.
steps.why: The book writes that the infrared is reflected back by the clouds and gases. The correct mechanism is absorption and re-emission: the gas molecules absorb the infrared and radiate it again, part of it downward. Write absorb and re-emit — the book's word reflected describes the outcome, not the mechanism.
common_mistakes: Writing that the ozone layer causes the greenhouse effect. Ozone absorbs ultraviolet; the greenhouse gases are CO₂, CH₄, N₂O and water vapour.
Saying the gases block the incoming sunlight. The gases act on the outgoing infrared, not on the incoming visible light.

recall.must_convey: That greenhouse gases such as CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O absorb the infrared and re-emit part of it back to the surface.
accept: part of it comes back to the surface

steps.memory_tip: Name the gas trio CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, then the verb pair absorb and re-emit.

steps.label: The surface temperature rises
lines: The returned radiation keeps the surface
warmer than it would be without these
gases, so the average surface temperature
of the Earth rises. A continued rise from
added greenhouse gases is called global
warming, which melts ice caps and raises
the sea level.
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Answer the asked contribution: the average surface temperature rises.
steps.why: This step answers the second half of the question. Without greenhouse gases the surface would settle well below its present average temperature; the returned infrared is what keeps the balance warmer.
common_mistakes: Ending at the mechanism and never stating the contribution. The question also asks what happens to the surface temperature: it rises.
Writing only a list of disasters. First state the physics — the average surface temperature rises — then name global warming.

recall.must_convey: That the effect raises the average surface temperature of the Earth, and a continued rise is called global warming.

steps.memory_tip: End with the asked sentence: the average surface temperature of the Earth rises.

insider_note: Four sentences carry the four marks: the definition, sunlight in and infrared out, the gases absorbing and re-emitting, and the temperature rise. The book says reflected back; write absorb and re-emit.
